decisions.context: The system must recreate forecasts for any past week. The brief does not specify a storage mechanism, so this ADR uses data versioning as the grounded design choice.

alternatives.label: Data version repository
cons: Small team: adds a repository to manage

alternatives.label: Data versioning in code repository
pros: Small team: keeps data versioning near code
cons: Reproducibility: may not suit large data

alternatives.label: No data versioning
cons: Reproducibility: cannot reliably recreate past inputs

decisions.rationale: Past-week reproducibility decides the choice: explicitly versioning data supports reconstruction. The cost is added repository management for a three-person team.
consequences: Record the data version used for each weekly forecast.
The design space has no sources or attested systems for this choice.

decisions.context: Weekly forecasts imply a recurring run, while the team also wants new model ideas to reach production quickly. The brief does not require continuous learning.

alternatives.label: Batch-based learning
pros: Weekly run: fits scheduled offline training
cons: Fast iteration: changes wait for a batch run

alternatives.label: Incremental learning
pros: Fast iteration: can incorporate data incrementally
cons: Weekly run: adds complexity to a simple recurring process

alternatives.label: Hybrid batch-based and incremental learning
cons: Small team: more training paths to maintain

decisions.rationale: Protecting the weekly run decides the choice: batch training fits the stated cadence and keeps the workflow manageable. The trade-off is that model changes wait for a batch cycle.
consequences: Run training on a schedule aligned with the weekly forecast.
The brief leaves the training-data cutoff and retraining cadence unspecified.

decisions.context: Model ideas should reach production quickly, but releases must not break the weekly run. The design space covers CI/CD scope and testing, but not a specific release safety mechanism.

alternatives.label: Build, test, and deploy models to be served and other system components
cons: Protect weekly run: deployment needs strong checks

alternatives.label: Build, test, and deploy machine learning pipelines and components needed during pipeline runs
pros: Protect weekly run: automates pipeline component delivery
cons: Fast iteration: does not explicitly cover served models

alternatives.label: No automated deployment
cons: Fast iteration: manual releases slow model ideas

chosen.label: Build, test, and deploy models to be served and other system components

decisions.rationale: Fast model iteration decides the choice: automate delivery of models and system components. This gives up some simplicity and makes release checks essential to protect the weekly run.
consequences: Include model and serving components in the automated delivery path.
Define release checks and recovery behavior; the brief does not specify them.

decisions.context: New model ideas must reach production without breaking the weekly forecast. The design space lists testing options, but provides no evidence passages or system attestations.

alternatives.label: Testing trained model quality
pros: Protect weekly run: checks model quality before release
cons: Small team: requires a defined quality criterion

alternatives.label: System integration testing
pros: Protect weekly run: exercises connected components
cons: Fast iteration: adds integration setup and runtime

alternatives.label: Canary testing
pros: Protect weekly run: limits initial exposure
cons: Small team: requires rollout and observation support

decisions.rationale: Protecting the weekly run decides the choice: check trained model quality before release. This requires the team to define acceptance criteria, and by itself does not validate pipeline integration or rollout behavior.
consequences: Set an explicit quality gate for candidate models.
Add integration or rollout checks if the weekly run requires them; the brief does not specify their form.

decisions.context: The system produces weekly demand forecasts, so its main pipeline needs a recurring trigger. The design space includes scheduled and manual triggers.

alternatives.label: On-schedule trigger
pros: Weekly run: runs on a recurring cadence
cons: Protect weekly run: requires failure handling

alternatives.label: On-demand trigger
pros: Small team: simple to start manually
cons: Weekly run: depends on an operator to remember

alternatives.label: On availability of new training data trigger
pros: Weekly run: reacts when data arrives
cons: Protect weekly run: arrival may not match weekly cadence

decisions.rationale: Protecting the weekly run decides the choice: a scheduled trigger directly matches the required cadence. The trade-off is that missed or failed runs need handling that the brief does not define.
consequences: Specify monitoring and recovery for missed or failed runs.

decisions.context: A broken weekly run would undermine the system, and new models will be released over time. The brief does not state what production signals to track.

alternatives.label: Model performance monitoring
pros: Protect weekly run: observes model performance
cons: Fast iteration: needs performance measures and labels

alternatives.label: Monitoring or logging data and predictions
pros: Protect weekly run: records inputs and outputs
cons: Small team: adds log storage and review work

alternatives.label: No in-production monitoring
cons: Protect weekly run: failures may go unnoticed

chosen.label: Monitoring or logging data and predictions

decisions.rationale: Protecting the weekly run decides the choice: logging data and predictions provides operational visibility even when forecast outcomes are not yet known. The cost is storing and reviewing those records.
consequences: Retain forecast inputs and outputs for operational review.
Choose retention, alerting, and privacy rules; the brief does not specify them.

uncovered: Data ingestion and source quality controls
Failure alerting, recovery, and run ownership
